# ⚾ OPS+ & BABIP

## A Data Story in Baseball

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Why This Matters

-   OPS+ captures overall offensive value
-   BABIP reflects outcomes on balls in play
-   Together: signal vs. noise in hitting performance

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Key Question

> How much of offensive performance is skill vs. luck?

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Dataset Overview

-   League: MLB
-   Variables:
    -   OPS+
    -   BABIP
-   Goal: Understand relationship and variability

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## OPS+ Explained

-   Adjusted for park and league

-   100 = league average

-   

    > 100 = above average hitter

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## BABIP Explained

-   Batting Average on Balls In Play
-   Influenced by:
    -   Defense\
    -   Luck\
    -   Contact quality

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Hypothesis

-   Higher BABIP → Higher OPS+
-   But not perfectly (luck plays a role)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Visualization


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# (Paste your original plotting code here)
```
:::


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## What We See

-   Positive relationship\
-   Considerable spread\
-   Outliers matter

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Interpretation

-   Some players sustain high BABIP (skill)\
-   Others regress (luck)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Takeaways

-   OPS+ is more stable\
-   BABIP is more volatile\
-   Combining both gives better insight

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Final Thought

> Not all hits are created equal ⚾

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
